title: The bat and the ball
hook: A bat and ball cost $1.10; the bat costs $1 more. What is the ball's price?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Check an intuitive answer against both simultaneous price constraints.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Check an intuitive answer against both simultaneous price constraints.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy bat and ball total €1.10, with the bat €1 more. If the ball is five cents, what total do both prices give? Toy inputs A=[5, 100]; B=[10, 100].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[110, 105, 5], [120, 110, 10]]. Labels: Total cents, Bat cents, Ball cents.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Both the total-price constraint and the price-difference constraint must hold at once. The ten-cent alternative satisfies the difference only by making the total too large. Checking both equations exposes the intuitive shortcut.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Ball cents=10, Bat−ball cents=100. What is Total cents? Answer: 120.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Ball cents=10, Bat−ball cents=100. What is Total cents?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 120. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Only 17% of 3,428 people answered all three Cognitive Reflection Test questions right; most said the ball costs 10 cents (Frederick, 2005).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Check an intuitive answer against both simultaneous price constraints.
